is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae s.l. (page 1, Abstract).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study reports Vgsc L1014F (kdr-west) and Ace-1 G119S (page 2, Material and Methods; Table 1, page 5).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 1 (page 5) provides the frequency of kdr and Ace-1 mutations for four distinct localities.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from field sites in Malanville, Benin (page 2, Material and Methods).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an original research paper reporting new field data (page 1).

sub_country_location.evidence: The study specifies four distinct rice-growing sites: Bodjekali A, Bodjekali B, Toumboutou A, and Toumboutou B in Malanville, Benin (page 2, Material and Methods).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study was carried out from June to October 2022 (page 2, Material and Methods).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes a specific, new collection period (June-October 2022) in Malanville.

supplement.evidence: All necessary data, including site-specific frequencies, are provided in the main text and Table 1.

assessment.summary: This study investigated the impact of pesticide use in rice farming on insecticide resistance in Anopheles gambiae s.l. in Malanville, Benin. It reports resistance to DDT and pyrethroids, associated with high frequencies of the kdr L1014F mutation, and low frequencies of the Ace-1 G119S mutation.
